slides.headline: At the trial, she was the one they tortured. Then she painted this
slides.sub: Artemisia Gentileschi, Judith Slaying Holofernes, c. 1620

slides.headline: Rome, 1611
slides.text: Artemisia is 18, already a gifted painter. Her teacher, Agostino Tassi, assaults her.

slides.headline: She takes him to court
slides.text: The trial lasts seven months. To test her word, the court tortures her, not him.

slides.headline: They bind her fingers
slides.text: Cords are tightened around a painter's fingers. She keeps repeating her story.

slides.headline: And he walks free
slides.text: Tassi is convicted and banished from Rome. The sentence is never carried out.

slides.headline: So she picks up her brush
slides.text: Her Judith is no delicate heroine. She holds him down like it's work.

slides.headline: And she is not alone
slides.text: Her maid pins Holofernes to the bed. Two women, acting together.

slides.headline: Look closer
slides.text: Many see in his face the man who hurt her, and in Judith, Artemisia herself.

slides.headline: In the end, she won
slides.text: She became the first woman in Florence's academy of art. He is remembered only because of her.
